title: tenant-egress-escrow-iac-safety-circuit
author: Asha Menon
body:
Overview

This document defines the Tenant Egress Escrow pattern: a Terraform-first, policy-gated module and operational playbook that prevents tenant workloads from causing uncontrolled outbound bandwidth or billing spikes during large evals, DB dumps, or third-party data transfers. It is intended for multi-tenant GPU fleets, CI/eval sandboxes, and partner integrations where egress and IP/egress routing must be budgeted and safely throttled.

Goals

1) Provide a reusable Terraform module that creates a tenant-level egress escrow: a scoped NAT/Egress bucket, metering rules, and an active safety circuit that trips and isolates a tenant when thresholds are exceeded.
2) Ensure the module is CI/CD gated with unit and integration tests, and that deployments include canary and rollback playbooks.
3) Offer operational runbooks for oncall to diagnose and remediate egress escalations with minimal disruption.

Scope and non-goals

- In-scope: GCP and AWS NAT/Egress proxy patterns, Terraform module API, GitHub Actions gating, instrumentation metrics, alerting thresholds, tenant lifecycle steps.
- Out-of-scope: tenant billing UI changes, legal approvals for cross-border transfers, per-tenant data classification.

Rationale

We observed two recurring operational incidents in 2024: large eval jobs that pulled tens of GBs of third-party datasets causing surprise egress bills, and misconfigured CI jobs that leaked test artifacts to public buckets. The Escrow pattern isolates and meters egress at the tenant boundary and provides an automated safety circuit to stop exports when thresholds are crossed.

High-level design

1. Terraform module (tenant-egress-escrow): responsible for creating:
   - a dedicated NAT Gateway / Egress Proxy per tenant (or shared with quotas)
   - a rate-limited egress token bucket implemented in the proxy (envoy/nginx + rate-limiter)
   - CloudWatch/Stackdriver metrics + per-tenant budget alarms
   - an Escrow Controller (serverless function) that flips an isolation flag in tenant config when alarms fire
2. CI/CD safety: module PRs must pass unit plan checks, static checks (tflint/terrascan), and an integration test that deploys a per-PR ephemeral tenant and runs a synthetic egress load test against a sandbox NAT.
3. Runbook & oncall: clear alerting with remediation steps and a single-click rollback path (revert to previous NAT config or deny egress ACL).

Terraform module interface (recommended fields and semantics)

| Input variable | Type | Default | Description |
|----------------|------|---------|-------------|
| tenant_id | string | n/a | Unique tenant identifier (used in resource names and metrics) |
| egress_quota_gb | number | 10 | Soft quota in GB per 24h window before safety circuit engages |
| burst_allowance_gb | number | 2 | Short-term burst allowance within the 24h window |
| nat_type | string | "proxy" | One of ["proxy","nat-gateway"] - proxy mode supports fine-grained throttles |
| shared_pool | bool | false | If true, uses shared NAT pool with tenant tagging |
| alert_email | string | "infra-oncall@redwood.ai" | Escrow alarm notification target |

Example usage (minimal)

```hcl
module "tenant_egress" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood/terraform-modules.git//tenant-egress-escrow?ref=v0.2.1"
  tenant_id = var.tenant_id
  egress_quota_gb = 20
  burst_allowance_gb = 5
  nat_type = "proxy"
  shared_pool = false
  alert_email = "infra-oncall@redwood.ai"
}
```

Operational metrics and alerts

- Metric: tenant.egress.bytes_window24h (gauge)
- Metric: tenant.egress.burst_bytes_5m (gauge)
- Alert: egress_quota_breach WARNING when bytes_window24h > egress_quota_gb * 0.9 -> notify slack #infra-alerts / Page (P2)
- Alert: egress_quota_breach CRITICAL when bytes_window24h > egress_quota_gb -> trigger Escrow Controller and Page (P1)
- Alert: egress_burst_exceeded when burst_bytes_5m > burst_allowance_gb -> throttle token issuance, no page (informational)

Escrow Controller behavior (summary)

- On CRITICAL alarm: controller sets tenant.status.egress_isolated = true and writes a tenant note with cause and timestamp. It also posts to #tenant-ops and opens a ticket in the tenant's Jira project if configured.
- On periodic reconciliation (every 15m): controller evaluates the rolling 24h window and will automatically lift isolation when bytes_window24h < egress_quota_gb * 0.5 for 24h AND manual review flag is removed.

CI/CD and testing strategy

1) Pre-merge checks for module PRs:
   - terraform fmt + validate + tflint + terrascan (policy-as-code)
   - terraform plan with mock vars and snapshot compare for resource churn
   - unit tests for module input validation (Terratest or kitchen-terraform)
2) Integration test (runs in ephemeral environment per PR):
   - deploy module with small egress_quota_gb=1 into sandbox project
   - run synthetic egress generator container (curl loops to external object store)
   - verify metrics ingestion and that CRITICAL path transitions the test tenant to isolated state
   - teardown must fully destroy ephemeral resources (no leftover NATs or addresses)
3) Canary promotion pipeline: staging -> canary tenants (5 tenants) -> global rollout. Promotion requires manual approval and at least 48h of egress telemetry.

GitHub Actions snippet (example test job)

```yaml
name: Module Integration Test
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  integration-test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Setup Terraform
        uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v2
      - name: Run tflint and terrascan
        run: tflint && terrascan scan -i .
      - name: Deploy ephemeral tenant
        run: |
          terraform init -input=false -backend-config="bucket=${{ secrets.SANDBOX_BACKEND }}"
          terraform apply -auto-approve -var="tenant_id=pr-${{ github.run_id }}" -var="egress_quota_gb=1"
      - name: Run egress load generator
        run: ./tools/egress-generator --target http://example-public-blobstore --bytes 40MB
      - name: Validate isolation
        run: ./scripts/check-tenant-isolated pr-${{ github.run_id }}
      - name: Destroy ephemeral
        if: always()
        run: terraform destroy -auto-approve -var="tenant_id=pr-${{ github.run_id }}"
```

Runbook: egress surge / billing alert (oncall)

Priority: P1 (billing risk, possible external exposure)

1) Triage (first 10 minutes)
   1. Acknowledge page and open a short incident note.
   2. Query recent metrics: tenant.egress.bytes_window24h and tenant.egress.burst_bytes_5m for the tenant_id.
      - CLI example (metrics API):

      `redwood-metrics query "tenant.egress.bytes_window24h{tenant_id=\"tenant-123\"}" --window 24h`

   3. Check Escrow Controller logs to see whether controller already isolated the tenant.
   4. If isolation not active and bytes_window24h > quota -> trigger manual isolation via the admin CLI: `redwood-admin tenant isolate --tenant tenant-123 --reason "egress_quota_exceeded"`

2) Containment (10–30 minutes)
   - Apply a temporary deny egress ACL for non-essential destinations using the per-tenant ACL module:

     `terraform apply -auto-approve -var="tenant_id=tenant-123" -target=module.tenant_egress.tenant_acl`

   - If traffic is from a CI job, identify the job id and stop the runner or kill the pod.
   - Add the tenant to the incident ticket with notes and current egress totals.

3) Root cause and recovery (30–120 minutes)
   - Determine source: eval job, CI artifact leak, or scheduled export. Check job traces, recent PR merges, and K8s pod logs.
   - If export was accidental, ask tenant owner to run an internal purge and to request a quota uplift if required.
   - Decide: keep isolation for automated cooling period (default 24h) or lift early after manual verification.

4) Post-incident
   - Create a retro in the incident log with cost impact and corrective actions.
   - Suggested corrective actions: tighten default egress_quota_gb for new tenants to 5GB, add a synthetics regression that replays previously failing pattern, and add a per-tenant pre-approval step for exports > 50GB.

Ownership and escalation

- Module owner: infra/terraform team (primary: @asha-menon)
- Escrow Controller owner: eng-platform (primary: @marcus-li)
- Pager: infra-oncall rotation (primary contact listed in oncall roster)
- Billing follow-ups: finance-legal -> billing@redwood.ai

Rollout checklist (recommended)

1. Merge module v0.2.1 with automated tests green.
2. Deploy to staging and enable telemetry for 72h.
3. Run synthetic flood tests against staging NATs and confirm controller behavior.
4. Create migration plan for existing tenants: prefer gradual opt-in for first 100 tenants, with conservative quotas.
5. After 14 days of canary monitoring, promote to global.

Security considerations

- Escrow Controller must run with least privilege: ability to annotate tenant rows and update feature flags only. Do NOT grant broad write access to tenant storage.
- Logs containing exported URIs must be redacted before storing in long-term logs.

Appendix: Sample diagnostic commands

- List tenants currently isolated:
  `redwood-admin tenant list --filter egress_isolated=true`
- Inspect per-tenant egress in the last 1h:
  `redwood-metrics query "tenant.egress.bytes_window24h{tenant_id=\"tenant-123\"}" --window 1h`
- Force-lift isolation (requires approval):
  `redwood-admin tenant unisolate --tenant tenant-123 --approval ticket-456`

Diagram (textual)

[Client Pod] -> [Tenant egress proxy (envoy+rate-limiter)] -> [NAT / Public Internet]
                                       |-> Metrics exporter -> Monitoring
                                       |-> Escrow Controller (subscribe alarms)
